detail.title: Operational Foundations of Causal Memory (Revised)
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes the criteria for causal memory, establishing that a persistent state only functions as memory when it provides predictive sufficiency or control utility relative to a specific coarse-grained model. Physical memory systems are bounded by the information-theoretic cost of maintaining these states against dissipation, with non-driven passive degrees of freedom modifying the effective entropy production rate.
detail.reason: Integrating new findings on coarse-graining and Langevin dynamics refines the operational criteria.

detail.title: Thermodynamics and Nonreciprocal Information Engines
detail.summary: We find that non-reciprocal couplings and non-driven passive degrees of freedom significantly alter the entropy production bounds of information engines. Predictive power is bounded by the ability of the system to maintain causal states, where dissipation is minimized when state transitions align with the driven dynamics.
detail.reason: Refining the role of non-driven degrees of freedom provides a more accurate view of dissipation bounds.
